## 9917c0a4fb29

**Reproduced missing semantic branch, supported by canonical examples.** The
ordinary generator places sources only to the left of a full-height color-9
vertical guide. In 600 default draws, zero contain a right-side source. The
canonical rule actually reflects cells in either direction into empty in-bounds
targets; all three canonical pairs require right-to-left filling. Racket matches
all three; the independently coded left-only rival fails all three. Missing
zero-based coordinates are train 0 `(2,0)`, train 1 `(3,2)`, and test 0
`(1,3), (5,1), (7,4)`; exact pairs and comparisons remain in the audit JSON.

Exact 5×9 self-check-accepted counterexample:

```text
0 0 0 0 9 0 0 0 0
0 0 0 0 9 0 0 0 0
0 0 0 0 9 0 3 0 0
0 0 0 0 9 0 0 0 0
0 0 0 0 9 0 0 0 0
```

Racket changes row 2 to `0 0 3 0 9 0 3 0 0`. A left-only copier leaves it
unchanged, missing `(2,2)`. The remaining rows stay unchanged. Evidence includes
input, complete authority output, rival output, source hash, and self-check in
`checks/audits/9917c0a4fb29.json`, witness `missing_right_to_left_branch`.

This rival does **not** fit canonical demonstrations; that is precisely why the
missing branch in ordinary generation is important. It is different from the
canonical-fitting shortcut in the primary task. The right-to-left witness was
constructed for the audit, not emitted by the ordinary generator.

**Suggested repair, not applied:** add right-only and bilateral source examples,
then cover occupied-target and out-of-bounds behavior separately. Revise the
left-only summary. Do not weaken or rewrite the correct canonical authority to
match the generator's narrower distribution. Those additional branch tests are
recommendations, not work claimed complete here.
